Rashi on Berakhot 10a:10:1.hebrew: סמוכים לעד לעולם - בדברי תורה כתיב, [אחרי] "נאמנים כל פקודיו" — "סמוכים": סמיכת כל פקודיו עשוים באמת וישר, ולצורך, ולא דבר רק:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:10:1.english: [They are] juxtaposed forever and ever - This is written concerning the words of the Torah: [after] "All His precepts are sure," [it says,] "they are juxtaposed" — the juxtaposition of all His precepts is made in truth and uprightness, and for a purpose, and not an empty thing.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:11:1.hebrew: כלום יש עבד שמורד ברבו - ויבא להכחיש את דברי הנביא:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:11:1.english: Is there a slave who rebels against his master - And [thereby] come to deny the words of the prophet.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:11:2.hebrew: אמור לו כלום יש בן כו' - והא חזינן הכא דהוה:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:11:2.english: Say to him: Is there a son, etc. - And behold, we see here that there was [one].

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:11:3.english: So too here, it was - It will ultimately be.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:12:1.hebrew: ואמר שירה - כנגד כולם אמר שירה, לכששרתה רוח הקודש עליו:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:12:1.english: And said a song - Corresponding to all of them, he said a song when the Holy Spirit rested upon him.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:13:1.hebrew: וכל קרבי - על שם קרבי אמו, שדר בתוכן:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:13:1.english: And all my innards - On account of the innards of his mother, in which he resided.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:1:1.hebrew: פתח באשרי וסיים באשרי - אלמא חדא היא, דאשרי כל חוסי בו סיומא דלמה רגשו גוים הוא:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:1:1.english: He opened with "Happy is" and concluded with "Happy is" - It follows that [these two psalms] are one, for "Happy are all who take refuge in Him" is the conclusion of "Why do the nations rage" [Psalm 2].

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:20:1.english: From where is it inferred - That it was stated with regard to the day of death.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:21:1.hebrew: בא וראה וכו' - הוא סבר דהכי בעי: מאי שנא קרבים דנקט:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:21:1.english: Come and see, etc. - He thought that this is what he was asking: What is different about "innards" that [the verse] mentioned [them]?

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:24:1.hebrew: חמשה ברכי נפשי - לעיל חשיב להו:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:24:1.english: Five [instances of] "Bless [the Lord, O] my soul" - Earlier, [the Gemara] enumerated them.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:26:1.hebrew: מאי דכתיב מי כהחכם ומי יודע פשר דבר - משום דאיירי בסופה בסמיכת גאולה לתפלה, נקט ליה:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:26:1.english: What is [the meaning of] that which is written: "Who is like the wise man, and who knows the interpretation of a matter" - Because at its end it deals with juxtaposing redemption to prayer, [the Gemara] cited it.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:26:2.hebrew: דאשכחן דאזל אליהו לגבי אחאב - דכתיב: וילך אליהו להראות אל אחאב:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:26:2.english: For we find that Elijah went to Ahab - As it is written: "And Elijah went to appear to Ahab."

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:26:3.hebrew: יהורם אזל לגבי אלישע - כשהלכו על מואב הוא ויהושפט (במלכים ב ג). דמתוך שלא היו הולכים זה אצל זה, לא היה מוכיחו על שלא נשא אשה:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:26:3.english: Yehoram went to Elisha - When he and Jehoshaphat went against Moab (in II Kings 3). For since they were not going to one another, [Isaiah] was not rebuking [Hezekiah] for not having married a woman.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:29:1.hebrew: כבשי דרחמנא - סתרים דהקב"ה, כמו "רישא בכבשא" (חולין ד' צג:) — בהטמנת האפר:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:29:1.english: The secrets of the Merciful One - The secrets of the Holy One, Blessed be He; like "a head in kivsha" (Chullin 93b) — [referring to] burying in the ashes.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:2:2.hebrew: חטאים כתיב - קרי ביה חטאים, שיכלה יצר הרע:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:2:2.english: "Sins" is written - Read it as "sins," so that the evil inclination will cease.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:30:1.english: A decree has been decreed - That you shall die.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:31:1.hebrew: מקובלני מבית אבי אבא - דוד, שראה את המלאך וחרבו שלופה בידו בסוף ספר שמואל (ב כד), ולא מנע עצמו מן הרחמים:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:31:1.english: I have received [a tradition] from the house of my father's father - [This refers to] David, who saw the angel with his sword drawn in his hand at the end of the Book of Samuel (II Samuel 24), and did not prevent himself from [praying for] mercy.

Rashi on Berakhot 10a:3:1.hebrew: שפיל - השפיל עצמך לסוף המקרא. כל דבר שהוא בסוף קרוי שפילו של דבר:
Rashi on Berakhot 10a:3:1.english: Go down - Lower yourself to the end of the verse. Anything that is at the end is called the bottom of a thing.

Tosafot on Berakhot 10a:1:1.hebrew: כל פרשה שהיתה חביבה על דוד כו' - וא"ת: מאי "כל הפרשיות"? והא לא אשכחן שום פרשה אחרת שמתחלת באשרי ומסיימת באשרי, אלא היא! וי"ל: דלאו דוקא פתח באשרי וסיים באשרי, אלא חתימה מעין פתיחה — כמו תהלה, שפתח בתהלה וסיים בתהלה: "תהלת ה' ידבר פי"; וכן הרבה פרשיות שמתחילות בהללויה ומסיימות בהללויה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 10a:1:1.english: "Every chapter that was dear to David, etc." - And if you say: What is [the meaning of] "all the chapters"? For behold, we do not find any other chapter that begins with Ashrei and concludes with Ashrei except this one! And one can say that it does not strictly mean [that he] began with Ashrei and concluded with Ashrei; rather, [it means] a conclusion resembling the opening — such as [the psalm of] Tehillah, where he began with "tehillah" and concluded with "tehillah": "My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord" (Psalms 145:21); and similarly, many chapters begin with "Hallelujah" and conclude with "Hallelujah".
